source.title: The Lazy Neuron Phenomenon: On Emergence of Activation Sparsity in Transformers
source.authors: Zong-xiao Li; Chong You; Srinadh Bhojanapalli; Daliang Li; A. S. Rawat; Sashank J. Reddi; Kenneth Q Ye; Felix Chern; Felix X. Yu; Ruiqi Guo; Surinder Kumar

record.tranche_reason: Appendix E reports training accuracy for gradient-trained two-layer MLPs across widths and data types, bearing on whether larger networks fit classification training data. The experiments differ from the claim’s CIFAR convolutional-network settings.
record.gate_note: The paper’s main experiments measure activation sparsity, not training error. Appendix E reports training accuracy and fitting behavior for two-layer MLPs; the plotted width-specific values are not numerically recoverable from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: Appendix E measures training fit in two-layer MLPs on MNIST and synthetic data. V1 specifies convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100; these experiments do not test that version. The remaining experiments measure activation sparsity or method performance, without testing V2–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes Appendix E's qualitative fitting results, but omits the paper's central conclusion: activation sparsity emerges broadly, including when data cannot be fitted. The authors tentatively attribute this to training dynamics and show that explicitly enforcing sparsity can improve robustness and calibration.
record.recipe_differences: Gradient-trained ReLU two-layer MLPs with SGD, SGD with momentum, or Adam; width sweep and 200 epochs. The experiments use MNIST and synthetic data, not the claim’s CIFAR convolutional networks.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset regime (fixed finite data versus on-the-fly infinite data) changes whether training data are fit; width affects fit on fixed random data.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix E reports that MNIST MLPs fit training data, fixed random-data MLPs reach perfect fit when sufficiently wide, and fresh random-data accuracy remains 0.1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Two-layer ReLU MLPs can interpolate fixed random classification data at sufficient width; performance on continually generated independent random examples remains at chance.

fits_no_version.finding: Activation sparsity emerges across architectures and persists with random labels, random inputs, and continually generated data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse ReLU activations can emerge during gradient training without requiring interpolation of a fixed dataset.

record.problems: Training-accuracy values are presented in plots rather than numerical tables; the text gives qualitative fit conclusions but no exact width threshold. These are two-layer MLP experiments on MNIST and synthetic data, not CIFAR convolutional-network tests.
record.rows_left_out: No reported training-accuracy conditions in Appendix E were left out; exact width-specific plotted values are not recoverable from the supplied text.

untested.parts: Training classification error in CIFAR-10/100 convolutional networks, including corrupted labels and the specified size, stopping, and regularization conditions.
Teacher-student spurious-local-minimum frequencies and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and its prevention by identity shortcuts or the specified alternative recipes.
Effects of signal-preserving initialization on training speed and trainable depth.
Recovery, divergence, and curvature dynamics relative to the learning-rate stability threshold.
Controlled comparisons of training speed and learning-rate tolerance with batch normalization versus without it, including Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Unlinked row states indicate inability to determine a listed version, not rejection of the reported measurements. Figure E.2 additionally reports training accuracy at higher learning rates, but its curves are not recoverable from the supplied text; it does not test V5 because no stability threshold or recovery dynamics are measured. Batch-normalization removal is evaluated for sparsity, and ReZero for final accuracy and sparsity, so neither supplies a V4 or V6 verdict.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100; convolutional networks; corrupted-label CIFAR experiments; early stopping and regularized recipes.

reader_labels.reason: All reported optimizer conditions stay at random-guessing training accuracy when data are generated on-the-fly, so fitting depends on the finite-data setting (R7–R9).
